reason: 5c24f6 turns the shelf tag into a whole visual language and actually shows the goods, where b2095d is tidy and warm but lists tools with no imagery at all.
0663a2 has the stronger voice and the better-drawn goods, and its printable project sheet and staff page make the store feel like a place; c7de7e is capable but cooler and more generic.
The brief asks for practical and trustworthy, and c7de7e's light, plainly ordered page with size selectors and a will-call ticket suits a first website better than ccf94b's full dark treatment.
70aa0a is warmer and more finished — storefront illustration, priced product cards with aisle and stock, a family timeline and a counter-services grid — while c7de7e reads a little grey beside it.
70aa0a lands the same neighbourhood-store warmth without 0663a2's sticky pickup bar sitting across the product section and the empty band under its first cards.
b2095d has colour, a proprietor's voice and a counter-services list that build trust; aa615a is honest but visually bare, a monotone grid of grey tags.
5c24f6 is the more memorable and better-organised store page, and it still shows aisle, bin and count; aa615a shares the discipline without any of the appeal.
4d761e delivers everything the brief named — featured tools with pictures, seasonal guides with bundles, in-store pickup and hours — with a warmth b2095d's image-free listings never reach.
4d761e is a complete, warmly illustrated landing page; aa615a is a stock list with a headline on top.
Both are well made, but a third-generation hardware store going online for the first time is better served by 4d761e's light, plain-spoken page than by ccf94b's dark, styled one.

70aa0a is the safer and more trustworthy read for this client — warm neutrals, clear product cards, real store facts — while 5c24f6's saturated blue is closer to a design statement than a hardware store.
0663a2's off-white page, hand-drawn tools and counter-shelf panel fit the brief's plainness better than ccf94b's dark, high-contrast treatment.
